biomarker_label: Homologous recombination deficiency / BRCA1 / BRCA2 pathogenic variant (germline and somatic)
relevance_rationale: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is one of the tumor types where homologous recombination deficiency changes treatment, and olaparib maintenance is approved in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. BRCA1/2, PALB2, and ATM status also governs whether platinum stays in the plan, and disease in the 50s raises the prior for an inherited variant.
status_evidence: profile.json:biomarkers[7] 'Germline findings (incidental)' value 'none detected, per incidental germline reporting on the tumor NGS report', confirmation_status ngs_pending
profile.json:biomarkers[] reports KRAS, TP53, and KMT2C from the December 2025 tumor NGS; no BRCA1/2, PALB2, ATM, or genomic-instability score appears either way
hardening_gap: Incidental germline reporting on a tumor NGS report is not a germline panel: it is not designed for germline sensitivity, it misses large rearrangements, and the report on file does not state which homologous-recombination genes were sequenced. Closing this takes a dedicated germline multigene panel on blood or saliva covering BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, ATM, CDKN2A, STK11, and the mismatch-repair genes, plus somatic HR gene coverage and a genomic-instability score on whatever tumor NGS is run next.

recommended_assay.test_name: Dedicated germline multigene panel (BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, ATM, CDKN2A, STK11, MMR genes) on whole blood or saliva
recommended_assay.tissue_required: whole blood or saliva; no tumor tissue and no biopsy
recommended_assay.bundled_with: one blood draw shared with germline multigene panel and HLA class I typing; somatic HR gene calls and a genomic-instability score ride on the recurrent-lesion comprehensive NGS

therapeutic_implication.approval_status: FDA approved 27 December 2019 for maintenance in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma without progression on at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum
therapeutic_implication.notes: BRACAnalysis CDx is the companion diagnostic. A somatic-only BRCA finding does not satisfy the germline-defined label and reflexes to germline confirmation.

rationale: Germline status here rests on incidental reporting from a tumor NGS report, which is not a substitute for a germline panel, and guidelines call for germline testing in every patient with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. A pathogenic BRCA1/2 or PALB2 variant would put an approved PARP-inhibitor maintenance strategy on the table in this tumor type, argue for keeping platinum in the sequence, and change screening for relatives. Most patients test negative, and this is a blood draw with no biopsy attached, which is why it should go out now rather than wait on tissue.
references: guideline:NCCN Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment: Breast, Ovarian, Pancreatic, and Prostate v2.2026
notes: The POLO maintenance label is written for disease that has not progressed on at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum, so this patient's recurrence four months after adjuvant FOLFIRINOX does not map onto it cleanly. The germline result still governs later-line PARP-inhibitor use, platinum re-challenge, and family testing, so the mismatch is a reason to read the result carefully, not a reason to skip the test.

relevance_rationale: CLDN18.2 is expressed in roughly half to two-thirds of pancreatic adenocarcinomas and is the strongest surface handle this case has. The tumor stained 2+/3+ in 60% of cells on the resected primary.
status_evidence: profile.json:biomarkers[0] CLDN18.2, '2+/3+ membranous staining in 60% of tumor cells (resected primary, December 2025 specimen)', confirmation_status confirmed
profile.json:biomarkers[1] 'CLDN18.2 (recurrent lesion)' not assessed, confirmation_status ihc_pending

hardening_gap: Three things sit between this stain and an eligibility call. The result is 60% of tumor cells at 2+/3+, below the >=75% used in SPOTLIGHT and GLOW. The antibody clone and assay were not named, so it is not known whether this was the VENTANA CLDN18 (43-14A) RxDx assay that defines that cutoff. And the tissue is the December 2025 resection, not the recurrence that emerged after ten cycles of FOLFIRINOX. Re-staining with the CDx assay, ideally on recurrent-lesion tissue, closes all three at once.

recommended_assay.test_name: CLDN18.2 IHC by the VENTANA CLDN18 (43-14A) RxDx assay, or the sponsor assay named by the trial being screened for
recommended_assay.tissue_required: recurrent-lesion biopsy preferred; the archival December 2025 resection block is an acceptable fallback
recommended_assay.turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks once tissue is in hand
recommended_assay.bundled_with: recurrent-lesion biopsy: one pass supplies comprehensive DNA plus RNA tumor NGS and a block for the IHC stains below

therapeutic_implication.approval_status: FDA approved 18 October 2024 with fluoropyrimidine and platinum chemotherapy
therapeutic_implication.notes: Label covers CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma at a >=75% 2+/3+ cutoff on the 43-14A CDx assay. Use in pancreatic adenocarcinoma is off-label on both the tumor type and the percentage.

rationale: The tumor is CLDN18.2-positive but at 60% of cells rather than the >=75% used in the registrational trials, on an unnamed assay, and on tissue that predates ten cycles of FOLFIRINOX. A 60% result is a weaker predictor of benefit than a >=75% result would be, and expression is patchy enough within a tumor that one archival block may not describe the recurrence. Re-staining, ideally on a recurrence biopsy, decides whether the CAR-T, ADC, and bispecific programs that set their own lower cutoffs are reachable, and it is the assay this case turns on.
notes: CLDN18.2 CAR-T, ADC, and bispecific programs set their own eligibility thresholds, several of them lower than 75%, and each names the assay it accepts. The threshold that matters is the one in the protocol being screened for, not the zolbetuximab label. Whether CLDN18.2 expression holds through chemotherapy is not established, which is the second reason the recurrence, not the primary, is the tissue to stain.

rationale: HER2 has never been stained in this case, and an IHC 3+ result would open an approved tumor-agnostic ADC in a patient whose disease recurred four months after adjuvant chemotherapy. The honest expectation is a negative result, since only a small percentage of pancreatic adenocarcinomas are HER2 IHC 3+, but the stain is inexpensive, runs on tissue that already exists, and needs no new procedure. A 2+ result reflexes to ISH and does not qualify for the tumor-agnostic indication on its own.

A positive stain makes the mesothelin CAR-T, ADC, immunotoxin, and bispecific programs screenable, none of which is approved and several of which take pancreatic adenocarcinoma specifically. It costs one more stain on tissue that already exists, so the gap is cheap to close and awkward to leave open if cell-therapy trials are being considered.

rationale: No fusion result is on file, and whether the December 2025 panel covered fusions is not stated, so retrieving that report is the cheapest first move. TRK fusions in pancreatic adenocarcinoma are rare and are largely confined to KRAS wild-type tumors, and this tumor carries KRAS G12R, which makes a positive result very unlikely. It reads out at no extra cost on the RNA-capable panel already recommended for re-profiling the recurrence, so it does not justify a separate order.

Raise it only if a FAP-directed trial is in play, where its advantage is needing no biopsy.

rationale: TMB was 0.83 mutations per megabase against a threshold of 10, which closes the tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab route. The assay was not named, and TMB from a small targeted panel is not interchangeable between platforms, but that caveat bites at values near the cutoff and this one is more than an order of magnitude below it.
